title: Cycle Resource Optimizer and Triggered Scope Trims
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We need a lightweight, repeatable decision process and supporting tooling to dynamically slice cycle scope when mid-cycle signals indicate capacity shortfalls (unplanned attrition, larger-than-expected bugs, or priority customer escalations). This ticket defines an operational 'Cycle Resource Optimizer' (CRO) and a set of gated 'Triggered Scope Trim' rules that PMs can run to produce a deterministic trimmed plan with minimal debate.

Goals:
- Produce a small decision engine (spreadsheet + guidance) that translates live staffing and velocity signals into recommended scope reductions at the initiative and feature level.
- Standardize thresholds for when to invoke a trimmed flow (utilization above 90% for two weeks, >=2 high-sev incidents consuming >30% of eng capacity, or a sales-driven high-priority P0 request).
- Define microtranche slices per initiative so we can choose which subfeatures to postpone with minimal customer/regulatory impact.
- Track and record trade-offs and owner sign-offs for auditability and post-cycle learning.

Acceptance criteria:
- CRO spreadsheet that, given inputs (FTEs by role, current velocity points, open bugs capacity, committed PRs), outputs a ranked list of scope items to defer and estimated regained capacity in story points.
- Playbook and checklist (Confluence) for PMs to run the triggered trim, including stakeholder notification template and rollback criteria.
- 1 internal dry run has been executed with three initiatives (Console UX, Dedicated Autoscaling, Runtime Kernel Work) and results documented.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We want an automated ranking but must preserve safety: deferred items cannot include security/compliance hotfixes or SLO-critical work.
- Design/Research work is lower-latency to pause but may cause UX churn; include explicit UX debt tracking when deferring design tasks.
- Avoid cross-team fragmentation: prefer trimming peripheral subfeatures rather than core platform contracts to reduce integration drag.

Stakeholders: PM leads (Aisha Kumar, Marco Li), ENG leads (Sofia Gomez, Chen Wu), Design lead (Priya Shah), Customer Success (Elena Park).
updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: Aligned with PM leads on scope and thresholds; asked ENG to expose weekly utilization metric. Action: ENG to add utilization export to capacity sheet (due 2026-03-06).
2026-03-05 - ENG instrumented utilization export; initial numbers show two initiatives trending >88% utilization. Noted that incident queue consumed 18% of team points last sprint. Marked as watch.
2026-03-07 - Design input: Priya flagged three UX experiments that can be delayed with limited impact (estimated 8 story points each). Added to candidate defer list.

2026-03-08 - Dry-run planning meeting: selected three initiatives for simulated trim. CRO spreadsheet populated with live inputs; algorithm suggested deferring 14 story points from Runtime Kernel Work and 12 points from Console UX to restore 12% headroom.

2026-03-09 - Review: Stakeholders accepted simulated outcome with one caveat: Dedicated Autoscaling has an external dependency for a partner contract (risk if trimmed). Decision: mark partner-dependent items as protected. Added rule to blacklist items with external SLA dependencies.
2026-03-10 - Playbook draft posted to Confluence and shared with execs for review. Requested sign-off from Head of Eng for the first real invocation if thresholds cross.
decisions: Use 90% sustained utilization over two weekly samples as primary trigger for invoked trimming.
Protect security, compliance, and partner SLA-dependent work from automatic trimming; these require exec approval to defer.
Prefer deferring design experiments and non-core UX enhancements before pausing backend or runtime contract work.
Implement a mandatory stakeholder notification template and 48-hour cooling-off period before finalizing trims unless emergency (P0) is declared.
